title: Google wants to put AI data centres in space. Here’s how ‘Project Suncatcher’ will work
description: As power grids buckle under the weight of AI data centers and their incessant power needs, Google is looking to the heavens for answers. The artificial intelligence momentum has run into concerns of energy and resources. Training massive frontier AI models and powering billions of daily inference queries requires huge amounts of electricity and millions of gallons of water for server cooling. This puts pressure on natural resources and puts question on the feasibility of running AI sustainably. This is where Google comes in with a novel idea – take AI out of the Earth, quite literally.

title: Can AI chips survive in space? Google is about to find out
description: For years, the biggest constraint on artificial intelligence has been what happens on the ground. AI models need enormous amounts of computing power, and that means data centres need vast supplies of electricity, cooling systems and physical space. As demand for AI continues to grow, technology companies are beginning to look somewhere very different for the infrastructure they will need next that is above earth. Google is preparing to test whether some of that infrastructure could eventually operate in orbit. On October 1, the company plans to send a prototype satellite into low Earth orbit aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare mission.
